App.tsx.overview: Top-level route definition for Tiket.ku. Wraps the app in BrowserRouter and maps five paths to their pages, giving the guided tour its bird's-eye view of runtime structure. The file also carries commented-out imports and routes for the ticket, registration, and payment flows that are not yet wired into this MVP build.

sections.title: Imports and route setup
sections.explanation: Imports routing primitives from react-router-dom and the five active page components. The commented imports on lines 8-9 hint at the planned Ticket and RegisterForm routes; they are inert and should be read as roadmap notes, not live dependencies.

sections.title: App component and routes
sections.explanation: Renders BrowserRouter containing a Routes switch with paths for home, '/matchs', login, signup, and the OAuth callback. Each Route uses an element prop rather than children, the React Router v6+ convention. Commented route placeholders on lines 20-22 mark future form, payment, and ticket destinations; they do not participate in routing.

sections.title: Default export
sections.explanation: Default-exports App so main.tsx can mount it as the single root component.

main.tsx.overview: Application entry point referenced by the first tour step. Imports global styles and App, then mounts the React tree into the DOM element with id 'root'. StrictMode is enabled to surface unsafe lifecycles and side effects during development.

sections.title: Global imports
sections.explanation: Loads app.css first so Tailwind theme tokens and utility classes are available before components render. App is imported via the '@/' alias configured in tsconfig, while React APIs come from their packages. Order matters here only for readability; CSS is applied as a side effect regardless.

sections.title: Root mount
sections.explanation: createRoot targets document.getElementById('root') with a non-null assertion, trusting the Vite index.html template to provide the element. render wraps App in StrictMode, which double-invokes certain functions in development to expose impure code. BrowserRouter itself lives inside App, not here.

app.css.overview: Design-token source of truth for the project, highlighted in tour step 2. Uses Tailwind CSS v4's @theme block to declare brand, surface, ink, night, and semantic color tokens plus font, radius, spacing, and shadow scales. Additional @utility rules expose reusable typography classes, and the file ends with base styles for focus visibility and reduced motion.

sections.title: Font and Tailwind imports
sections.explanation: Pulls Inter and Fira Code from Google Fonts as external @import rules, then loads Tailwind via @import "tailwindcss". In CSS, @import statements must precede other rules, which is why fonts and Tailwind appear before @theme. The fonts are later referenced by the --font-* tokens.

sections.title: Theme color tokens
sections.explanation: The @theme block defines custom CSS variables that Tailwind v4 turns into utility classes. Brand blues, neutral surface/ink/night palettes, line colors, and Tiket.ku semantic colors such as --color-primary and --color-danger all live here. Centralizing them means components can use classes like bg-brand-blue or text-danger without ad-hoc hex values.

sections.title: Type, radius, spacing, shadows
sections.explanation: Declares font stacks, radius scale, spacing scale, and shadow tokens inside the same @theme block. --font-heading aliases --font-sans so headings inherit the body family. Note that --radius-base/sm/lg are not a simple ascending scale (10px, 12px, 14px), so read each token by name rather than assuming ordering.

sections.title: Typography utilities
sections.explanation: Tailwind v4 @utility rules create named classes type-display, type-h1 through type-h3, type-body, type-small, type-caption, and type-code. Each bundles font family, size, line height, and weight so JSX can apply one class instead of four. type-code is the only one using --font-mono.

sections.title: Base styles and accessibility
sections.explanation: Applies the sans font stack to :root, gives every focusable element a visible brand-blue outline, and honors prefers-reduced-motion by collapsing animations and transitions. These are global safeguards: the focus ring supports keyboard navigation and the media query prevents motion sickness for users who opt out.

lib/utiils.ts.overview: Tiny shared helper referenced in tour step 2. The cn function composes conditional class names with clsx then resolves conflicting Tailwind utilities with tailwind-merge. Nearly every shared UI primitive imports it to merge a caller's className with defaults. Note the directory name 'utiils' is misspelled consistently, so imports must match it exactly.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: clsx provides the ClassValue type and flattens conditional/array/object class inputs. twMerge from tailwind-merge drops earlier conflicting utilities so the last one wins, for example 'p-2 p-4' becomes 'p-4'.

sections.title: cn helper
sections.explanation: A single generic variadic function: clsx(inputs) builds the class string, twMerge normalizes it. Wrapping both in one helper keeps components free of merge details and is the standard shadcn/ui pattern for className props.

components/Alerts.tsx.overview: Toast-style alert component introduced in tour step 3. Renders a fixed-position notification with a variant-driven color scheme, an animated entrance/exit via framer-motion, a countdown progress bar, and an optional onClose callback fired after the exit animation finishes. Variants map to design tokens from app.css.

sections.title: Imports and types
sections.explanation: Imports cn, framer-motion primitives, and React hooks. AlertVariant is a string union of five supported styles; AlertProps makes variant and desc required while duration and onClose are optional. Keeping the union narrow means variantStyles can be exhaustively typed with Record.

sections.title: Variant style map
sections.explanation: variantStyles assigns four token-based classes per variant: text, border, background tint, and progress bar. Record<AlertVariant, ...> makes TypeScript require every variant, so adding a new one forces a style definition. The 'dark' variant uses ink/surface tokens instead of semantic status colors.

sections.title: State and auto-dismiss timer
sections.explanation: Selects styles for the current variant and initializes isVisible to true. A useEffect starts a setTimeout that flips isVisible to false after duration ms (default 5000), and the cleanup clears the timer if duration changes or the alert unmounts. Flipping the flag triggers the exit animation rather than removing the node immediately.

sections.title: Animated alert markup
sections.explanation: AnimatePresence keeps the motion.div mounted until the exit transition completes, then calls onClose via onExitComplete. The div slides in from x:300 and out to the same side with a 0.4s duration, carries role='alert' for assistive tech, and combines variant classes through cn. Inside, an info icon, the description text, and a manual close button are laid out with flex; clicking the button repeats the same isVisible(false) path as the timer.

sections.title: Countdown progress bar
sections.explanation: A second motion.div animates width from 100% to 0% over duration/1000 seconds with linear easing, visually mirroring the auto-dismiss timer. Its bar color comes from the same variant map, so the accent stays consistent across all alert types.

sections.title: Default export
sections.explanation: Default-exports Alerts; the components barrel re-exports it with 'export *', so consumers can import it from the shared module path.

components/Button.tsx.overview: Shared button primitive from tour step 3. Extends native button attributes with a required label and explicit type union, then folds a disabled-driven spinner and 'Loading...' text into the render. The cn helper merges caller classes and applies disabled styling, making it the standard submit/action button across pages.

sections.title: Imports and props
sections.explanation: Imports cn and ButtonHTMLAttributes. ButtonProps extends the native attribute set, so onClick, disabled, aria-* props, and other button behavior pass through without manual forwarding. It adds a required label string and narrows type to button/submit/reset.

sections.title: Component signature
sections.explanation: Destructures label, onClick, className (default empty), and type (default 'button'), collecting everything else in props. The default type prevents accidental form submission when the button is used for navigation or toggles.

sections.title: Rendered button
sections.explanation: cn merges base classes, the caller's className, and conditional disabled styles. type and onClick are destructured out of props, so the later spread cannot override them; remaining native attributes pass straight through. When disabled is true, a CSS-only spinning border and the literal text 'Loading...' replace the label, coupling loading and disabled into one state.

components/index.ts.overview: Barrel file described in tour step 3. Re-exports every shared UI component from a single module so pages can import several primitives in one statement. It contains no logic; adding a component to components/ requires adding a matching export line here for the barrel to stay complete.

sections.title: Alert and button exports
sections.explanation: Re-exports Alerts (default export made available through export *) and Button. The blank lines are formatting only. These are the primitives most pages reach for first.

sections.title: Remaining UI exports
sections.explanation: One export * line per component module, covering banners, dropdowns, feature cards, hero, footer, navbar, input fields, and schedule sections. export * forwards named exports only, so this line does not re-export default exports; modules such as Alerts.tsx that only use export default must be imported directly from their own path. Worth noticing when a page imports a default-exported component elsewhere in the codebase.

components/InputField.tsx.overview: Form input primitive covered by tour step 3. Combines a native input with a CSS-only floating label, inline error text, password visibility toggle, and an optional forgot-password link. It uses the same disabled-driven styling discipline as Button and relies on Tailwind peer-* classes instead of JavaScript for the label motion.

sections.title: Imports and props
sections.explanation: Imports cn, lucide eye icons, React state, and router Link. InputFieldProps extends native input attributes and adds labelName, optional error, a narrowed type union, required boolean, and optional forgot-password controls. Extending native props means react-hook-form's register output can be spread onto the input unchanged.

sections.title: State setup
sections.explanation: Destructures props with defaults: empty className, text type, and '#' for forgotPasswordPath. showPassword tracks the toggle state, and isPassword is derived from type so password-only UI is gated by a single boolean.

sections.title: Input and floating label
sections.explanation: The input's effective type switches between text and password based on showPassword. cn merges base styles, caller classes, error red border, and disabled cursor. The adjacent span is the label: peer-placeholder-shown and peer-focus utilities move it down or up, which is why the input needs placeholder support to trigger the collapsed state. A required asterisk is appended inline.

sections.title: Password visibility toggle
sections.explanation: Rendered only for password inputs. The button is type='button' to avoid submitting a surrounding form, and its onClick is dropped when disabled. Eye/EyeOff icons reflect state, and aria-label changes between 'Hide password' and 'show password' for screen readers.

sections.title: Error slot and forgot-password link
sections.explanation:
A permanent

reserves vertical space for the error message, using a non-breaking space when there is no error so layout does not jump. For password fields only, a right-aligned area renders either a router Link to forgotPasswordPath or an empty placeholder paragraph. The Link's onClick prevents navigation when disabled, keeping the visual and functional disabled states consistent.

components/Features.tsx.overview: Landing-page section highlighted in tour step 4. Holds a static array of four value propositions and renders each through FeatureCard inside a responsive grid. Copy is in Indonesian per project convention, and headings use ink tokens from the design system.

sections.title: Imports and feature data
sections.explanation: Imports four Font Awesome icons and the local FeatureCard component. The features array stores icon elements plus title/description strings for schedule browsing, tribun selection, simulated payment, and QR e-tickets. Keeping content as data makes the JSX a simple map and would allow future localization without changing markup.

sections.title: Section heading
sections.explanation: The exported Features component renders a section with a subtle surface background, centered heading, and supporting paragraph. max-w-2xl keeps the text block readable while mx-auto centers it.

sections.title: Feature card grid
sections.explanation: A responsive grid goes from one column on mobile to two on sm and four on lg. Each item is mapped to FeatureCard with a stable key of f.title and explicit icon/title/description props; spreading the object could be shorter but naming props documents the card contract.

components/Hero.tsx.overview: First visible landing section in tour step 4. Renders a dark gradient hero with the Tiket.ku headline and two call-to-action buttons whose behavior is supplied by the parent through callbacks. The component is purely presentational: no routing or auth logic lives here.

sections.title: Imports and props
sections.explanation: Imports the shared Button and defines HeroProps with two callback functions: onPesanTiket and onLihatJadwal. Naming them in Indonesian matches UI copy while keeping the component decoupled from useNavigate. The parent decides where each action leads.

sections.title: Hero section shell
sections.explanation: The root section has id='main-content', the target of the skip link in Home.tsx. A decorative gradient overlay is marked aria-hidden so assistive tech ignores it. Content is centered with max-w-3xl; the eyebrow text names the venue, the h1 and subheading use display tokens, and the paragraph states the value proposition.

sections.title: Call-to-action buttons
sections.explanation: Two Buttons stack on small screens and sit side by side from sm upward. Each receives its label, the corresponding callback, and a className supplying colors, padding, and rounded corners. The secondary button uses line-on-dark plus a translucent hover, keeping visual hierarchy clear without another component variant.

components/SchedulePreview.tsx.overview: Landing-page event preview from tour step 4. Defines three hard-coded upcoming events and renders them as ScheduleCard components in a responsive grid. A single onDetail callback is forwarded to every card, so the parent controls navigation while this file stays presentational.

sections.title: Imports and sample events
sections.explanation: Imports ScheduleCard and declares a local events array of three objects with badge, title, subtitle, date, time, and venue. These are static marketing placeholders rather than Supabase data; the live match list lives in the Matches feature. Titles serve as React keys here, which is acceptable only because the sample list is fixed.

sections.title: Props interface
sections.explanation: SchedulePreviewProps exposes one required onDetail callback with no arguments. Because every card shares it, individual events cannot carry distinct destinations in this version.

sections.title: Schedule section and card grid
sections.explanation: Renders a white-background section with a centered heading and the same responsive grid pattern used by Features (1/2/3 columns). Each event object is spread into ScheduleCard and onDetail is passed through, keeping the preview free of layout duplication.

features/home/page/Home.tsx.overview: Landing page composed in tour step 4. Reads login state from useSession, defines navigation handlers, and assembles Navbar, Hero, Features, SchedulePreview, and Footer. It also includes a skip link for keyboard users and gates the 'Pesan Tiket' action behind authentication.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports the five landing sections via the '@/components' barrel, useSession for auth state, and useNavigate for routing. Using the barrel here shows the payoff described in tour step 3: one import path instead of five relative ones.

sections.title: Navigation handlers
sections.explanation: HomePage pulls navigate and isLoggedIn. handlePesanTiket redirects unauthenticated users to '/login' and otherwise goes to '/matchs'; handleLihatJadwal always goes to '/matchs'. This is the tour's auth-gating example: the decision lives in the page, not in Hero.

sections.title: Page composition
sections.explanation: A main wrapper holds a visually hidden skip link that becomes visible on focus and jumps to the Hero's '#main-content' id. Navbar receives the login boolean, Hero gets both handlers, Features is static, SchedulePreview reuses handleLihatJadwal for its onDetail, and Footer closes the page.

sections.title: Default export
sections.explanation: Default-exports HomePage for the '/' route in App.tsx.

features/matches/components/Card.tsx.overview: Renders a single match schedule card as a 3-column grid: home team, kickoff time and timezone, away team, plus a spanning footer with date and stadium. Combines MatchPayload data with an optional onClick handler from MatchCardProps.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports the MatchPayload type, TeamSection component, and MatchCardProps. Keeping these imports typed ensures the card stays aligned with the legacy match payload and shared prop contract.

sections.title: Match card layout
sections.explanation: Destructures home/away teams, match time, timezone, date, stadium, and onClick, then renders a CSS grid. TeamSection displays each side, the middle section shows kickoff time and timezone, and the bottom section spans all columns for date and stadium. The root div carries onClick so the whole card is clickable.

sections.title: Default export
sections.explanation: Default-exports MatchScheduleCard for consumption by the Matches page.

features/matches/components/TeamSection..overview: Small presentational component rendering a team's name and logo inside a centered section. It is used twice by MatchScheduleCard for the home and away sides.

sections.title: Import
sections.explanation: Imports TeamPayload, which defines the name and logo fields rendered by this component.

sections.title: Team section
sections.explanation: Accepts a TeamPayload and renders an uppercase team name plus logo image. The logo is constrained to a fixed box and uses object-contain so differently sized logos stay consistent. The component is stateless and reusable for both teams.

features/matches/page/Matches.tsx.overview: Page component that fetches matches via useMatchData and renders a 3x3 grid of cards. It stores the selected match id in sessionStorage and navigates to the match form on click.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports navigation, the Card component, and the useMatchData hook used to load and display matches.

sections.title: Matches page
sections.explanation: Calls useMatchData to get matches, defines handleCardClick to persist selectedMatchId in sessionStorage and navigate to /matchs/{id}/form when an id exists, and maps each match to a Card with an onClick handler. The grid layout uses three columns and rows.

sections.title: Default export
sections.explanation: Default-exports the Matches page for routing in App.tsx.

features/matches/hooks/useMatchData.ts.overview: Custom hook that fetches matches on mount and exposes matches, loading, and error state. The Matches page currently consumes only matches.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Includes a source-path comment plus React hooks, the getMatches service, and the MatchPayload type used for state.

sections.title: useMatchData hook
sections.explanation: Initializes state for matches, loading, and error. The effect runs an async fetchData that calls getMatches, stores results, clears any previous error, and always resets loading in finally. An empty dependency array ensures a single fetch on mount, and all three values are returned to consumers.

features/matches/service/matchService.ts.overview: Adapter service converting EventRecord records from eventService into the legacy MatchPayload shape used by the match schedule UI. It is intentionally shallow, with an upgrade path to use EventRecord directly.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports getEvents from the events service and the MatchPayload type that the legacy UI expects.

sections.title: Adapter rationale
sections.explanation: A ponytail comment documents that this adapter is deliberately shallow to keep the old UI compiling, and points to using EventRecord directly once the schedule page is redesigned.

sections.title: getMatches
sections.explanation: Calls getEvents(), then maps each event to a MatchPayload. Home team uses event title and image, away team uses subtitle or title, time/date/venue are copied, and tickets is built from event categories. This keeps the legacy card UI working while the newer event model carries richer data.

features/matches/types/matchesPayload.ts.overview: Defines the MatchPayload interface describing a scheduled match: identifiers, home/away teams, time and timezone, date, stadium, and a ticket price/quota map.

sections.title: Import
sections.explanation: Imports TeamPayload used for the home and away team fields.

sections.title: MatchPayload interface
sections.explanation: Declares the fields consumed by the match card and schedule UI. tickets is a record keyed by category name with price and quota, mirroring the adapted event categories.

features/matches/types/matchesPayload.ty.overview: Defines the TeamPayload interface with name and logo fields used by match payloads and the TeamSection component.

sections.title: TeamPayload interface
sections.explanation: Declares the minimal team shape needed to render a team section: a display name and logo URL.

features/events/service/eventService.ts.overview: Supabase data access for events: defines row interfaces, maps database rows to EventRecord, builds an upcoming-event query with an optional type filter, and exposes getEvents and getEventById.

sections.title: Row interfaces
sections.explanation: Defines CategoryRow and EventRow matching the database columns returned by Supabase, including the nested ticket_categories array. These interfaces type the raw query result before mapping.

sections.title: mapEvent
sections.explanation: Converts an EventRow into an EventRecord, renaming snake_case columns to camelCase and deriving remaining as quota minus sold for each category. Null category arrays are normalized to an empty list.

sections.title: buildQuery
sections.explanation: Builds a Supabase query selecting events with their categories, filtering to events on or after today, and ordering by date then time. An optional EventType filter is applied when provided.

sections.title: getEvents
sections.explanation: Executes buildQuery, throws on error, and maps the returned rows to EventRecord objects.

sections.title: getEventById
sections.explanation: Reuses buildQuery, adds an id equality filter and single-row selection. A PGRST116 error is treated as not found and returns null; other errors are thrown.

features/events/types/event.types.ts.overview: Domain type definitions for the events feature: event types, category and event records, order item input, buyer input, and issued ticket shape.

sections.title: EventType
sections.explanation: Union type restricting events to football or concert.

sections.title: EventCategoryRecord
sections.explanation: Describes a ticket category including price, quota, sold count, and derived remaining availability.

sections.title: EventRecord
sections.explanation: Describes an event with schedule, venue, media, and its categories. This is the primary domain model used by services and UI.

sections.title: Order inputs
sections.explanation: Defines OrderItemInput for category/quantity pairs and BuyerInput for buyer identity fields used during registration and ordering.

sections.title: OrderTicket
sections.explanation: Describes an issued ticket with id, order id, QR code, and issuance timestamp.

lib/supabase.ts.overview: Creates and exports a singleton Supabase client from Vite environment variables, throwing if either required value is missing.

sections.title: Import
sections.explanation: Imports createClient from @supabase/supabase-js.

sections.title: Environment validation
sections.explanation: Reads VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY from import.meta.env and throws a clear Indonesian error if either is absent, prompting use of .env.local.

sections.title: Client export
sections.explanation: Creates and exports the shared supabase client used by all services.

features/auth/schema/authSchemas.ts.overview: Zod schemas for authentication forms: a base authSchema, a loginSchema alias, and a signupSchema with name and password confirmation, plus inferred TypeScript types.

sections.title: Imports and base field
sections.explanation: Imports zod and defines errorMessageInput as a non-empty string used as the starting point for validated fields.

sections.title: authSchema
sections.explanation: Validates email format and password length between 6 and 20 characters, with Indonesian error messages.

sections.title: loginSchema
sections.explanation: Aliases authSchema for the login form.

sections.title: signupSchema
sections.explanation: Extends validation with a name field restricted to letters and spaces, plus confirmPassword and a refine check ensuring passwords match.

sections.title: Inferred types
sections.explanation: Exports AuthSchema, LoginSchema, and SignupSchema inferred from the Zod schemas for use with react-hook-form.

features/auth/service/authService.ts.overview: Thin wrappers around Supabase auth: session retrieval, state subscription, user id requirement, email and Google sign-in, sign-up, sign-out, and mapping auth errors to Indonesian messages.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports the AuthError type and the shared supabase client used by all auth helpers.

sections.title: Session helpers
sections.explanation: getSession returns the current Supabase session, and onAuthStateChange subscribes to auth state changes using Supabase's callback type.

sections.title: requireUserId
sections.explanation: Fetches the current user and returns their id, or throws an Indonesian message prompting sign-in when no authenticated user exists.

sections.title: Email auth
sections.explanation: signInWithEmail delegates to signInWithPassword, while signUpWithEmail calls signUp with full name stored in user metadata.

sections.title: Google and sign-out
sections.explanation: signInWithGoogle starts Google OAuth redirecting to /auth/callback, and signOut ends the current session.

sections.title: mapAuthError
sections.explanation: Maps Supabase auth errors to Indonesian user-facing messages by checking known error strings, with a generic fallback. Covers invalid credentials, duplicate registration, unconfirmed email, weak password, OAuth, and network failures.

hooks/useSession.ts.overview: Custom hook that tracks the current Supabase auth session and loading state. It fetches the initial session on mount and subscribes to auth state changes, exposing isLoggedIn, isLoading, session, and user. It is referenced by the authentication service and session tour step.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports React's useEffect and useState along with the Supabase Session type. Pulls getSession and onAuthStateChange from authService so the hook stays a thin wrapper over the auth service.

sections.title: Session state and effect
sections.explanation: Initializes state with session null and isLoading true. On mount it fetches the current session, guards against updates after unmount with a mounted flag, and subscribes to auth state changes to keep session in sync. The cleanup unsubscribes the listener and flips mounted to false.

sections.title: Derived return values
sections.explanation: Destructures session and isLoading from state and returns isLoggedIn, isLoading, session, and user. Deriving isLoggedIn from !!session keeps consumers from handling null checks repeatedly.

features/auth/page/AuthCallbackPage.tsx.overview: Handles the OAuth redirect callback by checking the Supabase session and routing to the intended destination or back to login. It is a minimal effect-driven component with a spinner fallback. It relates to the authentication pages tour step.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports useEffect from React and routing hooks from react-router-dom. Imports getSession from authService to verify the redirected session.

sections.title: Callback redirect logic
sections.explanation: Reads the intended destination from location.state with a fallback to /matchs. On mount it calls getSession; if there is an error or no session it navigates to /login, otherwise to the intended route. A mounted flag prevents navigation after unmount.

sections.title: Loading spinner
sections.explanation: Renders a centered spinning indicator while the session check resolves. The component returns this UI for the brief async window before navigation occurs.

features/auth/page/LoginPage.tsx.overview: Login screen with email/password and Google sign-in forms, validation, and redirect handling. It uses react-hook-form with a Zod resolver and surfaces auth errors via Alerts. It is part of the authentication pages tour step.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports icons, form libraries, routing, shared UI primitives, the session hook, and auth schemas/services. Keeps the page wired to the same validation and auth helpers used elsewhere.

sections.title: State and form setup
sections.explanation: Initializes navigation, location, session status, alert state, and Google loading flag. Configures react-hook-form with zodResolver(loginSchema) and destructures register, handleSubmit, errors, and isSubmitting.

sections.title: Redirect when already logged in
sections.explanation: Effect redirects authenticated users away from the login page to the intended destination. It waits until isLoading is false to avoid premature redirects.

sections.title: Submit handlers
sections.explanation: onSubmit calls signInWithEmail and shows a mapped error alert on failure or navigates on success. handleGoogle triggers Google OAuth and manages its loading state, showing an alert on error.

sections.title: Login form UI
sections.explanation: Renders the gradient hero, Google button, divider, and email/password form with floating labels and inline errors. Disables inputs while submitting and shows a spinner on the Google button. Footer is rendered at the bottom.

features/auth/page/SignupPage.tsx.overview: Registration screen with name/email/password form, Google sign-up, and email verification feedback. It validates with signupSchema and checks the session after signup to decide between redirect and verification prompt. It is part of the authentication pages tour step.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports icons, form libraries, routing, shared UI, the session hook, and auth schemas/services including getSession for the post-signup check.

sections.title: State and form setup
sections.explanation: Initializes navigation, location, session status, alert state, and Google loading flag. Configures react-hook-form with zodResolver(signupSchema).

sections.title: Redirect when already logged in
sections.explanation: Effect redirects authenticated users away from the signup page. It waits for isLoading to finish before navigating.

sections.title: Submit handlers
sections.explanation: onSubmit calls signUpWithEmail with name, email, and password; on error it shows a mapped alert. On success it calls getSession and either navigates if a session exists or shows a success message asking the user to verify their email. handleGoogle starts Google OAuth and handles errors.

sections.title: Signup form UI
sections.explanation: Renders the hero, Google button, divider, and a four-field form (name, email, password, confirm password) with inline validation errors. Disables inputs while submitting and includes a link back to login.

features/orders/service/orderService.ts.overview: Order creation and payment completion via Supabase RPCs. createOrder requires an authenticated user and maps the buyer and items into RPC parameters; completePayment completes an order by id and method. It belongs to the payment form and order processing tour step.

sections.title: Imports and interfaces
sections.explanation: Imports requireUserId, buyer/order types, and the Supabase client. Defines CreateOrderInput, CompletePaymentInput, and CreateOrderResult interfaces that shape the RPC calls and returned data.

sections.title: createOrder
sections.explanation: Ensures the user is authenticated, then calls the create_order RPC with event id, mapped items, and buyer details. Throws on error or empty result and returns the order id and total amount.

sections.title: completePayment
sections.explanation: Calls the complete_payment RPC with order id and payment method. Throws on error and returns the resulting ticket id.

features/payment/components/PaymentMetho.overview: Selectable payment method button component with selected/hover styling and aria-pressed state. It is a small presentational component used by the Payment page. It belongs to the payment form and order processing tour step.

sections.title: Props interface
sections.explanation: Imports React and defines PaymentMethodsProps with label, value, selected, and onSelect. The icon prop is commented out, leaving only the label rendered.

sections.title: Selectable button
sections.explanation: Renders a button that calls onSelect with its value on click. Applies selected or unselected Tailwind classes and sets aria-pressed to reflect selection state. Exports the component as default.

features/payment/hooks/usePayment.ts.overview: Hook providing a react-hook-form instance configured with zodResolver and the payment schema. It keeps form setup reusable for the Payment page. It belongs to the payment form and order processing tour step.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports zodResolver, useForm, and the payment schema with its inferred type. These wire schema validation into react-hook-form.

sections.title: PaymentFormValidation hook
sections.explanation: Creates and returns a useForm instance validated by paymentSchema via zodResolver. Spreading methods keeps all form helpers available to callers.

features/payment/page/Payment.tsx.overview: Payment page rendering payment method options and a card details form, navigating to the ticket page on submit. It manages the selected method state and registers form fields. It belongs to the payment form and order processing tour step.

sections.title: Imports and constants
sections.explanation: Imports React state, routing, shared UI, PaymentMethods, and the usePayment hook. Defines the PaymentOption type and the PAYMENT_METHODS list with card and bank options.

sections.title: Component state and submit
sections.explanation: Initializes params, form registration, navigation, and selected method state. onSubmit is wrapped by handleSubmit and navigates to the ticket route using userId; the legacy user lookup is commented out.

sections.title: Payment form UI
sections.explanation: Renders the payment method buttons, four card detail InputFields with error messages, and a submit button. Passes selected state to PaymentMethods and updates it via onSelect.

features/payment/schemas/paymentSchema.t.overview: Zod schema validating payment form fields: cardholder name, 4-digit card number, CVV, and expiry. It is used by usePayment through zodResolver. It belongs to the payment form and order processing tour step.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports zod for schema construction. Single import keeps the schema module minimal.

sections.title: Schema definition
sections.explanation: Defines a reusable nonempty string helper and the paymentSchema object with regex and length rules for nameOnCard, cardNumber, cvv, and validTHRU. Error messages are in Indonesian.

sections.title: Type export
sections.explanation: Exports PaymentSchema as the inferred type of paymentSchema, giving the form a compile-time contract matching validation.

features/tickets/service/ticketService.t.overview: Fetches a ticket by order id from Supabase, mapping snake_case database columns to the camelCase OrderTicket domain type. It belongs to the buyer registration and tickets tour step.

sections.title: Imports and row type
sections.explanation: Imports OrderTicket type and the Supabase client. Defines TicketRow describing the selected columns id, order_id, qr_code, and issued_at.

sections.title: getTicketByOrderId
sections.explanation: Queries the tickets table filtered by order_id using single(). Returns null on PGRST116 (no rows), throws other errors, and maps the row to OrderTicket with camelCase fields.

features/users/components/TicketCard.tsx.overview: React component rendering a ticket tribune card with price display and quantity increase/decrease controls. It notifies the parent via onCountChange. It belongs to the buyer registration and tickets tour step.

sections.title: Imports and props
sections.explanation: Imports React, Control type, and UserSchema. Defines TicketCardProps including name, tribune, price, count, control, and onCountChange; the GetDatas import is commented out.

sections.title: Quantity handlers
sections.explanation: Destructures tribune, price, count, and onCountChange from props. handleDecrease decrements only when count is greater than zero; handleIncrease increments unconditionally.

sections.title: Card UI
sections.explanation: Renders the tribune name, price, and a stepper with minus, count, and plus buttons. Clicking the buttons updates quantity through onCountChange.

features/users/hooks/useUserRegister.ts.overview: Custom hook wrapping react-hook-form with zod validation for user registration form state. It provides default values for all fields. It belongs to the buyer registration and tickets tour step.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports zodResolver, useForm, and userSchema with its inferred type. These connect schema validation to form state.

sections.title: useUserRegister hook
sections.explanation: Creates a useForm instance with userSchema resolver and default values for fullName, identityNumber, email, gender, and tickets. Returns all form methods spread for convenient use in components.

features/users/schema/userSchema.ts.overview: Zod validation schema for the buyer registration form. It defines reusable nonempty string rules, then constrains name, identity number, email, gender, and ticket quantities. It is reused by useUserRegister and TicketCard, and belongs to the buyer registration and tickets tour step.

sections.title: Validation building blocks
sections.explanation: Imports z from zod and declares two shared nonempty string validators with distinct error messages. Splitting generic text and dropdown validation lets the object schema reuse rules while still giving field-appropriate messages.

sections.title: Buyer object schema
sections.explanation: Defines userSchema with field-level constraints: fullName allows letters and spaces only, identityNumber accepts digits only, email must be a valid address, gender uses the option validator, and tickets is a record of numeric quantities. Regex and built-in email checks encode the input contract before data reaches services, so invalid form values are caught at the UI boundary.

sections.title: Inferred TypeScript type
sections.explanation: Exports UserSchema via z.infer so TypeScript consumers derive their type from the runtime schema instead of maintaining a separate interface. This keeps validation rules and compile-time types in sync.

features/matches/components/matchesProps.overview: Defines the MatchCardProps interface carrying an optional onClick handler for match cards.

components/Navbar.tsx.overview: Sticky navigation bar with route links and auth buttons.
